transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what brings me in is that some evenings after work, especially if I’ve been really strict with what I ate all day, I end up eating way more than I planned. Like I’ll have dinner, and then it turns into cereal, crackers, leftovers, sweets… all within a couple of hours. It’s been bothering me.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during those evenings when you have a lot of extra food?
Not really. Once I get started, I keep going back into the kitchen even while I’m telling myself to stop. I don’t feel like I’ve got control again until I’m already uncomfortably full.
How do you feel about yourself after one of these episodes of eating a lot in a short time?

I feel pretty bad about myself afterward. It’s like if my clothes feel tight, especially before something important like a client lunch or a leadership meeting, I start thinking I look sloppy, and that people won’t take me seriously. Even though I know I’m still doing my job, it gets in my head.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after one of these episodes of eating a lot?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I haven’t really talked about that before. Afterward I mostly just feel awful and try to move on.
Do you ever use laxatives after one of these episodes of eating a lot?
I’m not sure. I don’t really keep track of it like that, and I don’t know that I’d say it’s a regular thing.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these episodes of eating a lot?
I don’t think so. I mean, I feel really upset afterward, but I don’t remember making myself throw up.
How often do these episodes of eating a lot in a short time happen?

For the past few months, it’s been happening most weeks. Usually it’s one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to, and then the next day I try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising longer.
Do you exercise more on the days after you eat a lot?

Yes. The next day I usually tell myself I’m making up for it, so I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll take a longer hike than usual. Sometimes I push harder at softball conditioning too, even if I’m already tired.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes, I think I am. Like, if my waistband feels tight before a client lunch or a leadership meeting, I start worrying I look sloppy, and that people won’t take me as seriously. I know I’m still doing my job, but it gets in my head.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after eating?
I… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t been making myself throw up after eating.
Do you use laxatives after eating more than you planned?
No, I don’t use laxatives for that. That’s not something I’ve done after eating too much.
How often do you skip meals to try to make up for eating a lot the night before?

For the past few months, it’s been most weeks. Usually there’ll be one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to, and then the next day I’ll skip breakfast or lunch, or try to exercise longer to make up for it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change, at least not anything that stands out to me.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you try to make up for eating a lot by skipping meals or exercising more the next day?

Yeah, I think so. After one of those nights, the next day I’ll tell myself I’m making up for it by skipping breakfast and lunch, or I’ll take an extra-long hike or push harder at softball conditioning, even if I’m already tired. It’s mostly because I don’t want to gain weight from it.
Do you think skipping meals or exercising more the next day actually helps you avoid gaining weight from the extra food you ate?

I guess I think it does, at least in the moment. Like the next day I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll take a longer hike or push harder at conditioning, even when I’m tired, because it feels like I’m making up for what I ate the night before.
Do you think the extra exercise or skipping meals the next day is to punish yourself or to burn off the extra calories from the night before?

It’s more to burn it off, I think. Like I’m trying to make up for what I ate the night before. So the next day I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll do a longer hike or push harder at conditioning, even if I’m already tired.
Is your main goal when skipping meals or exercising more after eating a lot to prevent weight gain or to compensate for the calories you consumed?

I’d say it’s mostly to compensate for what I ate. Like the next day I’ll think I need to make up for it, so I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or go on a longer hike, or push harder at softball conditioning even if I’m already tired.
How many times a week do you typically have these episodes of eating a lot in a short time?
Usually one or two nights a week. It’s been like that most weeks for the past few months, where I eat way more than I meant to in a short time.
Do you think that by exercising more or skipping meals the day after eating a lot, you are undoing the effects of what you ate?

Yes, that’s how it feels in my head. Like if I skip breakfast and lunch the next day, or take a really long hike, or push harder at softball conditioning even when I’m tired, I’m sort of undoing what I did the night before. Making up for it, I guess.
How often do you skip meals or exercise more after one of these episodes of eating a lot?
Most weeks, it happens after those nights when I eat a lot—usually once or twice a week. The next day I’ll skip meals or exercise longer to try to make up for it.
